title: The 8 Levels of Overpriced Hipster Coffee
house: A bustling neon-lit metropolis called Bean City where produce citizens hustle through morning commutes, sipping expensive artisan brews under digital status glows.
catchphrase: The number on your forehead never lies.

levels.name: Pip, 22, Dishwasher
levels.story: The 8 levels of overpriced coffee. Level 1. Two dollars and fifteen cents left in my checking account, and I am standing in line at Brewtopia trying to pretend I belong here. Step aside, kid, you are blocking the real customers who pay for organic oat milk foam art and imported vanilla pods. My chest tightens with humiliation as the entire café stares at the glowing red digits flashing above my eyebrows. People like you shouldn't even smell authentic espresso beans, let alone look at them. I reach into my pocket for loose change, praying for a miracle, but my fingers only brush against a rusted paperclip. Then the manager points toward the exit and bans me forever without a word of explanation. Don't walk away yet, kid. Take this pass and see what lies behind the kitchen doors. Suddenly, the front glass shatters as a delivery drone crashes into the street outside, distracting everyone. In that brief moment of total chaos, a hooded figure slips me a counterfeit VIP pass. You'll see how that changes everything in Level 2. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Sunny, 25, Barista
levels.story: The 8 levels of overpriced coffee. Level 2. Fourteen dollars and fifty cents per hour is all I make while pouring artisanal lattes for ungrateful snobs who wouldn't know hard work if it hit them. You call yourself a barista with that pathetic minimum wage number glowing on your forehead? My manager glares at me for accepting outside help and threatens to dock my weekly hours if I mispronounce a single order. Leave her alone, she works harder than anyone in this pretentious trap while carrying the whole shift. My back aches, my wrists are swollen from repetitive strain, and my rent is due tomorrow morning. Then the cafe doors swing open to reveal an unexpected visitor holding a federal audit warrant. Nobody move! We have reason to believe unregistered beans are being processed on these premises. All the chatter stops instantly as heavy footsteps echo across the polished tile floor. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Mason, 31, Marketing Lead
levels.story: The 8 levels of overpriced coffee. Level 3. Four thousand two hundred dollars a month sounds decent until rent eats half of it in Bean City and taxes swallow the rest. Four thousand? That is what my assistant makes for lunch money in a week without breaking a sweat. I grit my teeth and stare at my laptop screen, watching my savings account slowly bleed out while my boss demands impossible quarterly growth. Don't listen to them, Mason, you are doing great work despite the impossible corporate pressure. I take a deep breath, trying to calm my racing heartbeat before my next pitch presentation. Then my phone rings with an urgent call from human resources announcing sudden restructuring. Effective immediately, your entire team is being reassigned to the basement archives. The screen of my computer flashes red, locking me out of my main project files completely. You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Zara, 28, Influencer
levels.story: The 8 levels of overpriced coffee. Level 4. Three thousand two hundred followers on my lifestyle page, and people treat me like Hollywood royalty in this designer café. Three thousand followers? That is cute, I make that much every ten minutes in crypto dividends without lifting a finger. My chest burns with sudden public embarrassment as my ring light tripod gets knocked over by a clumsy busboy. Let me help you pick up your camera gear before someone steps on it and ruins your stream. I force a smile for my live audience while fighting back hot tears of frustration. Then my phone screen goes entirely black as my main account gets permanently suspended for policy violations. Your brand sponsorships have all been canceled. You don't exist in the algorithm anymore. A strange notification pops up claiming my identity has been flagged by municipal authorities. You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.name: Cleo, 26, Founder
levels.story: The 8 levels of overpriced coffee. Level 5. Forty-five thousand dollars in angel funding is all I have to launch my green-tech startup in Bean City before our runway ends. Forty-five grand? That wouldn't even cover my weekly parking fees downtown, let alone a real venture. My hands shake as I pull up my prototype demo on my tablet screen for the skeptical venture capitalists sitting across the table. Your algorithm is solid, Cleo, don't let the old money dinosaurs intimidate you with their shiny badges. I wipe my sweaty palms on my blazer, refusing to back down from their piercing stares. Then my laptop receives an encrypted notification containing an anonymous wire transfer confirmation. Check the sender address. Someone just bought a controlling stake in your company. The numbers on the screen keep climbing higher and higher until my breath catches in my throat. You'll see that in Level 6.

levels.name: Rex, 39, Executive
levels.story: The 8 levels of overpriced coffee. Level 6. Eighteen thousand five hundred dollars a month gives me total control over corporate acquisitions in Bean City and access to the executive lounge. Eighteen grand? That is my hourly dividend return before breakfast, so why are you even talking to me? My jaw tightens with sudden shock as my corporate expense card gets declined by the automated register with a piercing buzzer sound. Sometimes the penthouse view makes you forget how gravity works, boss, especially when the floor gives way. I look around the room, realizing that my power and status were nothing more than a temporary illusion. Then my private corporate phone starts buzzing nonstop with emergency alerts from the board of directors. Sir, your accounts have been frozen under suspicion of insider trading and market manipulation. A masked security team steps out from the shadows of the hallway, blocking all exits. You'll see that in Level 7.

levels.name: Duke, 45, Mogul
levels.story: The 8 levels of overpriced coffee. Level 7. Forty-five thousand dollars a day flows into my offshore accounts from real estate empire holdings across Bean City. Forty-five grand a day? That wouldn't even pay for my morning security detail or my private yacht maintenance fees. My chest tightens with sudden rage as my private banking app flashes a sudden asset freeze warning notice across the screen. Empire built on sand always washes away when the tide comes in, sir, and your tide is turning fast. I slam my fist against the mahogany table, sending my porcelain teacup shattering onto the floor. Then my private security guards rush toward my table with drawn weapons. Stand back, everyone! The federal authorities have jurisdiction over this entire property now. The glass walls of the VIP lounge begin to retract, exposing us to the roaring rain outside. You'll see that in Level 8.

levels.name: The Mayor, 60, Ruler
levels.story: The 8 levels of overpriced coffee. Level 8. The final level. Unlimited resources mean nothing when you realize every single coffee bean in Bean City is grown from the exact same soil of human experience. You dropped this outside, mister, and I think it belongs to the person who started this whole endless cycle. I look at his glowing red digits and remember every cruel thing that was ever said across these marble tables by people who thought numbers defined their souls. The number on your forehead never lies, but maybe the heart behind it tells a completely different story when the cups are finally empty. I take a step forward as the digital displays across the entire metropolis begin to flicker and reset to zero. Suddenly, every citizen in the café drops their cups simultaneously, turning to face the front entrance as a new dawn breaks. Look outside. The rain has finally stopped, and the numbers are completely gone. You won't believe what happens when the doors open wide. What topic should we explore next in Bean City?
